name: Krea
tagline: Manage real-time and batch generation workflows from user-owned models or APIs

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 100 compute units/day; full real-time models and limited image, video, 3D, lipsync, upscale and LoRA access.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 5,000 compute units/month; selected video models; LoRA training with up to 50 images; upscale to 22K.
tiers.notes: Annual-effective value is calculated from the official 'Yearly -40% off' label.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 20,000 compute units/month; all video models; Nodes/Apps workflow automation and Nodes Agent.
tiers.notes: Annual-effective value is calculated from the official 'Yearly -40% off' label.

tiers.name: Max
tiers.limits: 60,000 compute units/month at the displayed selection; unlimited relaxed generations; LoRA fine-tuning with up to 2,000 files.
tiers.notes: Other compute selections from 40,000 to 100,000 change the price.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 80,000 compute units/month at the displayed selection; up to 50 seats; LoRA training with up to 20,000 images; unlimited relaxed generation.
tiers.notes: Other compute selections from 20,000 to 1.5 million change the price.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom compute packages, spend controls, SLA, audit logs and support.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-40% shown on the yearly toggle)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Monthly subscription compute does not roll over. One-time compute packs expire after 90 days. Max and Business prices rise with the selected compute allowance; annual Business/Enterprise arrangements can roll unused compute for up to 12 months.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Krea, manage real-time and batch generation workflows from user-owned models or APIs. The hard boundary is proprietary real-time models, gpu fleet, enhancement stack, and creative tools, plus frontier models, compute, and data.
coreLoopDIY: Organize prompts and real-time or batch generation workflows, submit jobs to user-owned models or APIs, and keep outputs reproducible.
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-supplied generation API
whatYouLose: proprietary real-time models, GPU fleet, enhancement stack, and creative tools
replacementScope: local workflow manager, not a model replacement
ongoingBurden: GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Krea because the product value is the model and compute fleet, not the prompt box around it. The recurring cost buys GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Node-based open-source diffusion workflow engine with a large ecosystem.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: Real-time previews, batches and reusable model graphs; the workflow is yours, including the complexity.

facts.install: Windows or macOS desktop installer, Windows portable archive, or manual Python install on Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.engines: Local and downloadable image, video, audio, 3D, and text models including Stable Diffusion/SDXL/SD3.5, FLUX, Wan, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, and Mochi; optional API nodes connect to hosted providers
facts.dataFormat: Models, inputs, outputs, and workflow JSON live in the local ComfyUI data tree; generated media can embed workflow and seed metadata, while API nodes transmit selected inputs to their provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It can batch and reuse graphs, but its real-time canvas is more technical and generally less fluid than Krea's low-latency hosted interaction.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, enough VRAM and disk for multi-gigabyte models, and a working model/workflow must be chosen before useful output appears

alternatives.name: Krita AI Diffusion
alternatives.desc: Live painting, queued jobs and local models inside Krita; real-time creation without renting Krea's canvas.

facts.install: Install Krita, import the plugin ZIP through Krita's Python-plugin importer, then connect a managed/local ComfyUI backend or the optional cloud service
facts.engines: ComfyUI-based Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, ControlNet, IP-Adapter, inpainting, upscaling, and segmentation workflows, plus models offered by the optional Interstice cloud
facts.dataFormat: The working image remains a local Krita document with layers and masks; local backends keep models and outputs on the machine, while cloud mode sends the prompt and relevant image/layer data
facts.gapVsPaid: Live painting is strong, but it needs Krita plus a local or cloud backend and lacks Krea's seamless browser model switching and batch orchestration.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires Krita, the plugin, a multi-gigabyte ComfyUI model bundle, and enough GPU memory; the easier cloud path requires an account

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: Local and API-backed models in a desktop node canvas, with a sketch editor, reusable workflows and a timeline.

facts.install: Install the macOS .dmg, signed Windows .exe, or Linux AppImage; Docker Compose is available for self-hosting
facts.engines: Local Ollama, llama.cpp/GGUF, MLX, Nunchaku, Hugging Face, and diffusion/media models, plus BYOK providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, FAL, Replicate, KIE, ElevenLabs, and Hugging Face
facts.dataFormat: Workflows, projects, assets, files, provider settings, and vector indexes live locally in YAML, SQLite/SQLite-vec, and application storage; optional S3 or Supabase storage is supported, and cloud nodes transmit their inputs
facts.gapVsPaid: Its sketch editor and workflows are reusable, but real-time feedback and creator polish lag Krea's purpose-built canvas.
facts.setupBlocker: No useful model or provider is bundled: the user must add an API key or download a multi-gigabyte local model, and some local backends add a large Python/Conda environment

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a local workflow manager, not a model replacement DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Krea in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ComfyUI as a local worker, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize prompts and real-time or batch generation workflows, submit jobs to user-owned models or APIs, and keep outputs reproducible.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create prompt, negative-prompt, seed, dimensions, model, and workflow controls.
Submit jobs only to the local ComfyUI endpoint configured in .env.
Record exact generation parameters and workflow JSON beside every output.
Build a searchable contact sheet with compare, favorite, annotate, and rerun actions.
Support local image-to-image and mask inputs without uploading them elsewhere.
Show estimated VRAM needs and fail clearly when a workflow or model is missing.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out training a new frontier model.
Deliberately leave out copying a vendor's proprietary model or dataset.
Deliberately leave out public generation hosting and moderation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
